study.title: Optimization of DSA image data input to a machine learning aneurysm identifier
study.venue: Proc. of SPIE Vol. 11317, Medical Imaging 2020: Biomedical Applications in Molecular, Structural, and Functional Imaging

imaging.modality_detail: 2D DSA sequences of intracranial aneurysms (pre-/post-coiling and post-pipeline), flattened along the time axis
vendors: Canon Infinix-i Biplane (Canon Medical Systems Corporation)

annotation.annotator_expertise: Users with 1-year minimum exposure to analysis and evaluation of neurovascular angiograms

task.task_description: Semantic segmentation of the intracranial aneurysm sac on time-flattened DSA frames with an encoder-decoder CNN; comparison of four temporal flattening schemes (average, median, standard deviation, minimum) and class-activation map analysis of network saliency.
task.clinical_application: Automating aneurysm contouring for angiographic parametric imaging and quantitative aneurysm assessment

architecture_names: Global average pooling (GAP) layer for class-activation maps

temporal_evidence.quote: the frames in the DSA sequences were flattened along the time-axis when the IAs were fully opacified to create a single frame

method.class_imbalance_handling: Combined Dice loss and binary cross-entropy loss, stated as suited to large class-size imbalance
method.explainability_method: Class-activation maps (CAMs) via global average pooling layer

metrics.metric: Segmentation + CAM inference time per frame

G1.quote: caused by limited numbers of image data used to train the segmentation network

G3.quote: investigation into utilizing the entire un-flattened sequence for IA segmentation may yield superior segmentation results due to the contrast motion in and out of the IA sac not being averaged across

G5.quote: Our aneurysm labels were created by multiple authors, hence, this process is subject to intra- and inter-observer variability which may lead to the introduction of bias.

G7.quote: as a “black-box” technique, it does not allow users to understand which image features are most important

other_limitations: No actual true-negative images; true negatives created by cropping during augmentation may add bias
Spurious network activation outside the aneurysm sac
Reduced performance for small aneurysms located off the internal carotid artery
CAMs assessed only for average-flattened inputs
future_work: Automatic extraction of aneurysm morphology (dome-to-neck ratio, aspect ratio, neck size) from segmented masks
Investigate additional pre-processing such as bilateral filtering
Use the entire un-flattened DSA sequence for aneurysm segmentation
Optimize network input pre-processing to improve segmentation
Apply to aneurysm occlusion prediction and surgical guidance
